content_html:
A savings goal is easier to reach when you know the monthly number behind it. This calculator works in two directions: give it a target and a deadline and it finds the monthly deposit you need, or give it the amount you can save each month and it finds how long the goal will take. Both include interest on your balance and, if you choose, inflation.

How to use this calculator

  1. What do you want to find: choose the monthly deposit or the time to reach the goal.
  2. Savings goal: the amount you want to end up with, such as a down payment, an emergency fund or a car.
  3. Amount already saved: the money set aside for this goal today. It earns interest from day one.
  4. Annual interest rate or return: the APY of a savings account or CD, or an assumed average return if the money is invested.
  5. Time to reach the goal or monthly deposit, depending on the mode.
  6. More options: deposit at the start instead of the end of each month, and an inflation rate if your goal is in today's prices.

The formula behind it

Your current savings grow to S × (1 + i)n, where i is the annual rate divided by 12 and n is the number of months. The rest of the goal must come from deposits, and a series of equal monthly deposits grows to P × ((1 + i)n − 1) ÷ i. Setting the two parts equal to the goal and solving for P gives the monthly deposit. Deposits made at the start of the month earn one extra month of interest, so the required amount is slightly lower. With a 0% rate the answer is simply the remaining amount divided by the number of months.

To find the time, the calculator adds deposits and interest month by month until the balance reaches the goal, and reports the first month it gets there.

A worked example

You want $20,000 in 5 years, you have $2,000 saved and your savings account pays 4%. The calculator shows a monthly deposit of $264.83. Over the 5 years you put in $17,890 in total (including the $2,000 you started with) and earn about $2,110 in interest.

Switch the mode to "How long it will take" and enter $300 a month: the same goal is reached in 4 years and 6 months. If you instead set inflation to 3%, the $20,000 goal in today's dollars becomes about $23,185 in 5 years and the deposit needed rises to $312.88 a month.

Ways to reach a goal sooner

  • Automate the deposit on payday so the money moves before you can spend it.
  • Compare rates. High-yield savings accounts and CDs often pay more than a standard account, and the gap adds up over several years.
  • Add windfalls such as tax refunds or bonuses to the amount already saved and re-run the numbers.
  • Match the account to the timeline. For a goal only a few years away, a stable rate usually matters more than a higher but uncertain return.

Limits of this estimate

The calculator assumes a constant rate and identical monthly deposits. It does not include taxes on interest, account fees or rate changes. Savings account rates can move at any time, so check your progress against the year-by-year table now and then.

faq.question: How do I calculate how much to save each month for a goal?
faq.answer: Subtract what your current savings will grow to from the goal, then divide the rest by the growth factor of a monthly deposit series. The calculator does this for you, including interest; with no interest it is simply the remaining amount divided by the number of months.

faq.question: Does saving at the start of the month make a difference?
faq.answer: Yes, a small one. Each deposit earns one extra month of interest, so the monthly amount needed is slightly lower. You can switch the timing under More options.

faq.question: Should I adjust my savings goal for inflation?
faq.answer: For goals several years away, it often helps. If you enter an inflation rate, the calculator treats your goal as today's prices and raises it each year, so the result reflects what the goal is likely to cost when you reach it.

faq.question: What interest rate should I use?
faq.answer: For a savings account or CD, use its annual percentage yield. For invested money, use a cautious average return, and remember investment returns are not guaranteed from year to year.

faq.question: Why does the calculator say my goal will take over 100 years?
faq.answer: With no deposits and little or no interest, the balance may never reach the goal. Increase the monthly deposit or the rate to get a realistic timeline.
